name: hash-blake3-stream64k
algorithm: std BLAKE3, 32-byte output through the streaming state, fed 65,536-byte pieces (the last piece is the remainder) of splitmix64 bytes, one fresh state per pass, reps passes with a one-byte write-back (mk/hash-blake3-stream64k.mk); the input, passes and checksums of std-hashmod/hash-blake3, so the row compares the state with the one-shot.

skip.c: no std hash: C has no standard BLAKE3, 32-byte output
skip.rust: no std BLAKE3, 32-byte output: Rust std has none (only SipHash-1-3 in DefaultHasher); no crate stands in
skip.go: no std BLAKE3, 32-byte output: Go std has none (hash/maphash is a different, seeded hash); no module stands in

notes: Idiomatic standard library, the large-piece streaming case (file hashing with 64 KiB reads; review finding H2-4): Mk Blake3State.New/Bytes/Sum, Zig init/update/final. 65,536 is a multiple of the chunk, so after the first piece every piece starts on a chunk boundary and Mk's Bytes sends four whole chunks at a time through the 4-chunk std.simd leaf, as the one-shot does. Bytes per second = mib * 1048576 * reps / median.
Zig: std.crypto.hash.Blake3 update hashes whole chunks of a piece in @Vector lanes; Mk's state uses its 4-chunk Vec[u32, 4] leaf (std/hash/blake3_wide.mk).

Checksums: equal to std-hashmod/hash-blake3's (the same digests); the Mk (mk build --release) and Zig 0.17.0 (-O ReleaseFast -mcpu=x86_64_v2) columns printed them in `go run ./tools/bench verify -publish-size` (status/std-hash2.md, fix round). Written by the std-hash2 lane. Not published: no number here is a measurement.
